paragraphs.context: The endowed are all descended from the ten
paragraphs.mainIdea: The children of the Red King.
paragraphs.simple: All the endowed children come from the ten children of the Red King, a magician king who left Africa in the 1100s with three leopards.

background.note: A magician king from long ago. Each of his ten children got a small part of his magic and passed it down in their families.

paragraphs.context: A were-beast. He is descended from a tribe
paragraphs.simple: Asa comes from a tribe in the northern forests who kept strange animals. When evening comes, Asa can change into a beast.

paragraphs.context: Emma can fly. Her surname derives from the
paragraphs.simple: Emma can fly. Her family name comes from a Spanish swordsman from the city of Toledo. His daughter married the Red King, so he is an ancestor of all the endowed children.

background.note: An old city in Spain, famous for making fine swords.

paragraphs.context: The boa's skin was black and silver and its eyes like beads of jet.
paragraphs.simple: The Red King had a rare snake, a boa, with black and silver skin and shiny black eyes. It never stopped watching, so no thief or killer dared to come near. The king could speak its language and loved it like a friend.

background.note: A hard, shiny black stone used in jewelry. "Eyes like beads of jet" = small, shiny, black eyes.

paragraphs.context: One day while the king was absent on a hunting trip, his eldest son, Borlath, caught the boa in a net.
paragraphs.simple: The king's eldest son, Borlath, the cruelest man alive, caught the boa and tortured it until it became a killer that squeezed its victims to death.

paragraphs.context: The king's daughter, Guanhamara, horrified by the boa's
paragraphs.mainIdea: A spell that came too late.
paragraphs.simple: The king's daughter Guanhamara rescued the boa and tried to cure it with a spell. The spell only made its hug weaker: now its victims did not die, but became invisible.

paragraphs.context: When Guanhamara died, the boa fell into a
paragraphs.simple: When Guanhamara died, the boa dried up into something neither alive nor dead. Her daughters kept it in a jar of blue liquid with a little bird. Borlath stole the jar, and many years later Ezekiel Bloor brought the boa back to life. Now its skin is silvery blue.

paragraphs.context: Ezekiel was now a hundred years old. He
paragraphs.simple: Ezekiel, now a hundred years old, has always wanted to become invisible, but he is afraid the boa's hug cannot be undone. He is still looking for a way to make invisible people visible again. The boa waits in the dark attics of Bloor's.

paragraphs.context: Across the road, at number twelve, Benjamin Brown
paragraphs.simple: At dawn Benjamin sees Charlie's three great-aunts, Lucretia, Eustacia and Venetia, creep out of Charlie's house in black hooded coats, their heads close together like people planning something secret.

paragraphs.context: If only Charlie hadn't inherited such a strange
paragraphs.simple: Benjamin thinks that if Charlie had not inherited a strange gift, and if the aunts did not know about it, he might be safe. When your ancestor is a magician king, your family expects a lot from you.

paragraphs.context: Benjamin's parents were private detectives and they tried
paragraphs.simple: Benjamin's parents are private detectives, so they try not to be noticed. Sometimes they wear a false mustache or a wig as a disguise.

background.note: People who are paid to find out secret information or find lost things, not police officers.

paragraphs.context: The tall man was Paton Yewbeam, Charlie's great-uncle.
paragraphs.simple: Benjamin sees Charlie's great-uncle Paton leave in dark glasses with a white stick. Paton's lights explode, so he never goes out in daylight. He puts a wand in the back of his car.

background.note: A white stick is used by blind people. Paton is not blind; it is part of his disguise in the light.

paragraphs.context: "Sort of," said Benjamin. "I've got some amazing
paragraphs.simple: Benjamin wakes Charlie very early with amazing news: he is going to Hong Kong.

background.note: A big city in southern China, on the coast. At the time of the story it was well known to British people because Britain ruled it until 1997.

paragraphs.context: "Er — no," said Benjamin. "He'd have to
paragraphs.simple: Runner Bean would have to be kept away from people and animals for a long time, and he would hate that.

background.note: In the past, dogs taken into Hong Kong or Britain had to live in a special kennel for months, to stop the spread of the disease rabies.

paragraphs.context: As Charlie began to splutter his protests, Benjamin
paragraphs.simple: A very rich Chinese man has asked Benjamin's parents to find a stolen necklace. The job may take months, so Benjamin is going too, but Runner Bean cannot.

paragraphs.simple: Grandma Bone bangs around the kitchen in her gray bathrobe. Suddenly she turns and says she can smell a dog.

paragraphs.context: My sisters are up to no good. Heard
paragraphs.simple: Paton heard his sisters making plans in the night. He has gone to stop them, because otherwise someone very dangerous will arrive. He hopes to be back in a few days.

paragraphs.simple: Charlie's mother rushes off to work at the market, but she looks too smart for selling vegetables. Charlie wonders if she has a boyfriend, and hopes not, for the sake of his lost father.

paragraphs.context: Charlie took her advice. When Runner Bean had
paragraphs.simple: Charlie plays with Runner Bean in the garden, using a slipper that Charlie hates because his name is sewn on the front.

paragraphs.context: Aunt Venetia suddenly said, "Tah dah!" and opened
paragraphs.simple: Venetia opens the door as if a queen or film star is coming in. It is the prettiest girl Charlie has ever seen, with golden curls, blue eyes and lips like an angel.

paragraphs.context: "Hello, Charlie!" The girl held out her hand
paragraphs.simple: The girl holds out her hand as if she expects a boy to kneel and kiss her fingers. Her name is Belle.

paragraphs.context: So it seems, thought Charlie. He went to
paragraphs.simple: Grandma Bone orders a special lunch for Belle: soup, cold ham and salad, and Maisie's Bakewell tart. Maisie answers rudely, calling her "Your Highness".

paragraphs.context: Charlie continued. "Bloor's is a big gray building

background.note: A punishment: a pupil must stay at school after classes or miss free time.

paragraphs.simple: Charlie remembers from his French lessons that "belle" means beautiful.

background.note: In French, "belle" means "beautiful". It is also a girl's name.

paragraphs.context: Charlie only just stopped himself from mentioning his
paragraphs.simple: Charlie nearly mentions his secret visit to his great-grandfather. Because of a family quarrel nobody explains, the visit must stay secret, so he tells another lie.

background.note: A long quarrel between members of a family. Grandma Bone and her sisters do not visit their father.

paragraphs.simple: Belle keeps staring at Charlie with dark green eyes. Paton went away to stop someone dangerous from coming. Charlie wonders: is that person already here?

paragraphs.simple: Charlie warns Runner Bean that if he is not quiet, it will be the end for him, and pulls a finger across his throat.

paragraphs.context: Charlie was amazed. His grandmother always had a
paragraphs.simple: Grandma Bone always has a nap after lunch, but she quickly takes Belle home. The girl seems to have some kind of power over her.

paragraphs.simple: Charlie did not practice in the holidays, so his trumpet playing is terrible. Old Mr. Paltry hits his knuckles and shouts in a squeaky voice.

paragraphs.simple: Madame Tessier shouts at Emma in English with a strong French accent.

paragraphs.simple: Emma leads Charlie to the small, dirty room where Manfred once locked her up. It has green slime on the walls and filthy blankets.

paragraphs.context: They chased the footfalls down the passage, up
paragraphs.simple: The children follow the footsteps to a long room full of empty jam jars and comics, with a bed, an oil lamp, a big cabinet and a desk under a skylight.

paragraphs.simple: The Bloors tried to make Ollie visible again with horrible drinks and smelly liquids, even spiderwebs on his bed.

paragraphs.simple: Ollie tried to escape once, but people walked into him and screamed, and he could not get out of the main doors, so he came back.

paragraphs.simple: Mr. Boldova pretends he sent the children to look for his escaped rat, Rembrandt.

paragraphs.simple: Ollie has run away and may now be locked in. Manfred watches Charlie suspiciously. He saw Charlie look at Selena Sparks's portrait, and he knows Ollie's toe is visible.
